questions.q: What Roman building type was used for legal gatherings and civil discussions?
questions.n: In Roman architecture, the basilica served as a large public building for legal proceedings and business transactions.

questions.q: In Roman urban planning, where are the market and city center typically located?
questions.n: The Forum was the central hub of Roman political, judicial, and commercial life.

questions.q: What Roman structure is semicircular and used specifically for entertainment purposes?
questions.n: Roman theaters were semicircular structures designed for plays and choral performances.

questions.q: What is a Roman structure that is dedicated specifically to deities?
questions.n: The temple was the primary religious structure dedicated to the gods or deified emperors.

questions.q: Conservation and Heritage: The development of Casa Manila is an example of what conservation approach?
questions.n: Casa Manila repurposes the historical domestic architectural style for modern educational and cultural use.

questions.q: What is the primary challenge when retrofitting heritage buildings?
o: High cost of skilled manual labor
Difficulty to insert new utility systems in old structures
questions.n: Heritage structures often lack the space or structural flexibility to accommodate modern MEPF systems without damaging historical fabric.

questions.q: How do architects typically balance preservation and modernization in heritage sites?
questions.n: Adaptive reuse allows for modern functionality while respecting and preserving the historical envelope.

questions.q: During the American colonization, what was the purpose of the 1.2m gap under the bahay na bato?
o: Para hindi nila magamit as storage for animals (To prevent its use as animal storage)
To provide space for outdoor storage of farming equipment
To protect the wooden structure from groundwater and floods
To allow for better air circulation and cooling
questions.n: The American colonial health authorities introduced this gap to improve sanitation and prevent disease by discouraging animal housing below living quarters.

questions.q: Universal Principles of Design & BP 344: Providing a single accessible entrance for all users aligns with which principle?
questions.n: Equitable use ensures the design is useful and marketable to people with diverse abilities without segregating users.

questions.q: What principle is applied when a space is easily adaptable to any use or function?
questions.n: Flexibility in use means the design accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and methods of use.

questions.q: When you design with color coding so that the space is usable and navigable even without text or signage, which principle are you applying?
questions.n: This principle ensures that the use of the design is easy to understand, regardless of the user's language skills or concentration level.

questions.q: Which Universal Design principle is applied when installing railings and a zocalo to prevent accidents?
questions.n: Railings and curbs (zocalos) minimize hazards and the consequences of accidental or unintended actions.

questions.q: Which Universal Design principle is applied when panic doors are designed to be light and use lever-type handles?
o: Size and Space for Approach and Use
questions.n: This principle requires the design to be used efficiently and comfortably with minimum fatigue.

questions.q: What is the minimum length of a bath and toilet?
questions.n: Under the NBC, the minimum dimension for a room with a water closet and a shower is 1.2 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a room with natural ventilation?
questions.n: The National Building Code requires a minimum of 2.7 meters for the first story when natural ventilation is used.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height for a room with artificial (mechanical) ventilation?
questions.n: Rooms with artificial ventilation are permitted a lower minimum ceiling height of 2.4 meters.

questions.q: What is the minimum ceiling height required for a mezzanine level?
questions.n: The NBC allows for a minimum clear ceiling height of 1.8 meters for mezzanine floors.

questions.q: By how much must a vent shaft increase in size or area for every additional story?
questions.n: According to the NBC, vent shafts must increase in size by 0.10 square meters for each additional story.

questions.q: What is the classification of a 'Super' violation?
questions.n: In the context of the NBC administrative fines, the most serious category is termed a 'Grave Violation'.

questions.q: What is the estimated project construction cost (PCC) for a 7-storey nursing home with a 950 sqm total floor area?
questions.n: 950 sqm multiplied by a rate of 50,000 Pesos per sqm equals 47,500,000.

questions.q: What is the Recommended Basic Fee (RBF) if the scope of services includes both Architectural and Engineering (DAEDS)?
questions.n: DAEDS for this project is calculated at 7% of the 47,500,000 PCC, which equals 3,325,000.

questions.q: What is the Recommended Basic Fee (RBF) if the scope of services is for Architectural only (DADS)?
questions.n: DADS for this project is calculated at 4.2% of the 47,500,000 PCC, which equals 1,995,000.

questions.q: What percentage of the total RBF should the architect have already received upon completion of the Design Development Phase under Architectural services?
questions.n: The standard schedule of payment for architectural services allocates a cumulative 35% of the fee upon completion of the Design Development Phase.

questions.q: If the client increases the floor area by 390 sqm, what will be the new RBF for architectural services only?
questions.n: The new area (1,340 sqm) brings the PCC to 67,000,000. For projects over 50M, a lower percentage or specific step-down fee calculation applies, resulting in 2,712,000.

questions.q: What is the maximum administrative fine that can be imposed for a single violation under the National Building Code?
questions.n: The maximum administrative fine per violation under the current IRR of the NBC is 10,000.00 Pesos.

questions.q: What is the specific fine amount for a violation classified as 'Light'?
questions.n: Under the NBC Schedule of Fines, Light violations are penalized with exactly 5,000.00 Pesos.

questions.q: What is the specific fine amount for a violation classified as 'Less Grave'?
questions.n: Less Grave violations carry a standardized administrative fine of 8,000.00 Pesos.

questions.q: What is the specific fine amount for a violation classified as 'Grave'?
questions.n: Grave violations are penalized at the maximum administrative rate of 10,000.00 Pesos.

questions.q: If a person or entity is found to be constructing without a permit, what is the fine in addition to the base administrative penalty?
o: A surcharge or 'penalty' which can reach 100% of the building permit fees
questions.n: Constructing without a permit incurs a surcharge that can equal the total amount of the permit fees themselves.

questions.q: Which category does 'Failure to post Certificate of Occupancy' fall under, and what is its corresponding fine?
o: Less Grave Violation, fine of 8,000.00 Pesos
questions.n: The failure to display the required certificate is considered a minor administrative oversight, thus a Light Violation.

questions.q: Which category does 'Use or occupancy of a building without a Certificate of Occupancy' fall under, and what is the fine?
o: Serious Violation, resulting in a fine of 12,000.00 Pesos
Grave Violation, resulting in a fine of 10,000.00 Pesos
Light Violation, resulting in a fine of 5,000.00 Pesos
Less Grave Violation, resulting in a fine of 8,000.00 Pesos
questions.n: Using a building without the required final clearance is a more significant breach than simple paperwork errors.

questions.q: Which category does 'Unauthorized change in type of construction from more fire-resistive to less fire-resistive' fall under, and what is the fine?
o: Grave Violation, which carries a fine of 10,000.00 Pesos
Less Grave Violation, which carries a fine of 8,000.00 Pesos
Light Violation, which carries a fine of 5,000.00 Pesos
Structural Violation, which carries a fine of 20,000.00 Pesos
questions.n: Compromising the fire-safety rating of a building is a critical safety breach, classifying it as a Grave Violation.

questions.q: What is the fine for 'Change in existing use or occupancy without a Certificate of Change of Occupancy'?
o: Grave Violation, carrying a fine of 10,000.00 Pesos
Less Grave Violation, carrying a fine of 8,000.00 Pesos
questions.n: Changing the use of a building (e.g., residential to industrial) without approval creates major safety and zoning risks.

questions.q: What is the fine for 'Failure to provide or install appropriate safety measures for the protection of workers and the public'?
o: Light Violation, resulting in a fine of 5,000.00 Pesos
Less Grave Violation, resulting in a fine of 8,000.00 Pesos
Grave Violation, resulting in a fine of 10,000.00 Pesos
questions.n: This specific item in the NBC schedule of fines is curiously categorized as a Light Violation.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of the Philippine Green Building Code?
o: To replace the National Building Code (PD 1096)
To mandate that all buildings produce their own renewable energy
To strictly enforce the use of imported green technologies
To improve building efficiency by adopting management techniques that mitigate impact on health and environment
questions.n: The code aims to minimize a building's negative environmental impact through energy, water, and material efficiency.

questions.q: At what point of the building process does the Green Building Code apply to a project?
o: Retroactively to all existing heritage structures
During the design and construction phase of new buildings meeting TGFA thresholds
Only during the post-occupancy maintenance phase
Upon the sale or transfer of property ownership
questions.n: The code is enforced during the permit application and construction phase for qualifying large-scale projects.

questions.q: Which green building rating system was achieved by the Arthaland Century Pacific Tower, specifically in the 'Zero Carbon' category?
questions.n: Arthaland's tower was the first in the world to be certified Zero Carbon by the EDGE system.

questions.q: What are the three primary environmental impact areas addressed by Green Building regulations?
o: Structural Stability, Fire Safety, and Architectural Style
Indoor Acoustics, Exterior Landscaping, and Parking Ratios
Energy Efficiency, Water Efficiency, and Material Sustainability
Site Security, Property Value, and Tenant Demographics
questions.n: These three pillars form the core focus of most green building codes to reduce resource depletion.

questions.q: What specific architectural feature is used in tropical green buildings, like the Arthaland tower, to reduce solar heat gain while allowing natural light?
questions.n: External shading devices like fins block direct sunlight from entering the glass while maintaining transparency and light.

questions.q: In green building design, what type of glazing is used to minimize the transfer of heat into the interior?
questions.n: Low-E glass has a special coating that reflects infrared light while allowing visible light to pass.

questions.q: To comply with water efficiency standards, what is the maximum recommended flow rate for a high-efficiency water closet?
questions.n: Modern green standards typically cap toilet flushes at 6 liters (full flush) and lower for dual-flush systems.

questions.q: What is the primary benefit of 'Adaptive Reuse' in the context of sustainable urban development?
o: Lowers the density of the urban center
Ensures the building remains unoccupied to preserve its original air
Guarantees that no modern technology is added to the site
Reduces the need for new materials and energy by repurposing existing structures
questions.n: By reusing the 'embodied energy' of existing buildings, we avoid the carbon footprint of demolition and new construction.

questions.q: Which urban farming method involves growing plants in a nutrient-rich mist, significantly reducing water consumption?
questions.n: Aeroponics grows plants with their roots suspended in air, sprayed with a fine mist of nutrient solution.

questions.q: What sustainable material is often used for roof eaves and soffits due to its durability and moisture resistance?
questions.n: Ficem and aluminum are resistant to rot, termites, and moisture, making them ideal for exposed exterior soffits.

questions.q: In the context of the Green Building Code, what does 'STAS' (Solar Thermal Absorption Systems) aim to utilize?
o: Renewable energy from the sun to provide hot water or heating
Reflective coatings to bounce sunlight away from the building
Photovoltaic cells to generate electricity for lighting
questions.n: STAS uses solar collectors to heat water or air, reducing the electrical demand for water heaters.

questions.q: What type of lighting fixture is most energy-efficient for large office spaces to meet green building power density requirements?
questions.n: LED troffers provide high-quality illumination with the lowest power consumption per square meter.

questions.q: Why is the use of 'Low-VOC' (Volatile Organic Compounds) paints encouraged in green buildings?
o: To reduce the cost of the project by using fewer chemicals
To improve Indoor Environmental Quality (IEQ) by reducing harmful chemical emissions
To make the paint dry significantly faster in humid weather
To ensure the color does not fade under direct tropical sunlight
questions.n: Low-VOC paints release fewer toxic gases, protecting the respiratory health of building occupants.

questions.q: What are the three primary classifications of violations under the National Building Code (PD 1096)?
questions.n: These are the three specific tiers of administrative violations used to determine fine amounts in the NBC.

questions.q: In the case of a 'Super' violation, which fine is consistently applied as the maximum penalty?
questions.n: A 'Super' or Grave violation always hits the 10,000.00 Pesos administrative ceiling.

questions.q: What is the Recommended Basic Fee (RBF) percentage for Architectural services only (DADS) for a Group 1 building?
questions.n: For Group 1 (Simple) buildings, the Architectural-only fee starts at 6% of the PCC.
